issues.title: Add explicit local transports and a bounded Qt pipe client bridge
issues.body:
## Bounded result
Child of FND-012/#131. Make startup, discovery, the Python client and the app harness explicitly distinguish private Unix sockets from local Windows named pipes. Reuse QLocalServer/UserAccessOption and a small packaged QLocalSocket byte-stream helper for the Python Windows backend. Preserve the existing newline JSON protocol, authoritative commands, request identity and errors; no remote listener or additional third-party runtime.

## Acceptance
- Default pipe names use fresh instance UUIDs; reject remote pipe forms. Keep Unix private directory/socket behavior. Windows discovery access must fail closed with appropriate per-user ACLs; do not use POSIX chmod as evidence of Windows security.
- Publish transport/address metadata and preserve it through discovery, verification and harness routing; maintain legacy Unix socket compatibility. Resolve the helper from trusted installed/source locations, never a discovery-controlled executable path.
- Helper uses bounded input/output and one overall connect/write/read deadline. Python retains protocol and correlation validation. Preserve structured failures and multiple-instance/stale-discovery behavior.
- Proportional tests exercise actual helper/QLocalServer bytes, representative fragmentation/timeout/malformed/size/correlation failures and one real macOS app regression. Obtain native Windows non-GUI helper/pipe evidence before closing this child; compilation alone is insufficient. Any new hosted execution is manual and coordinated as a milestone, never per commit.

## Review and remaining parent gate
Astra reviewed this architecture on 2026-10-13 against public Qt documentation and CPython 3.12.10 source; detailed evidence stays external. CPython multiprocessing uses a different pipe framing/timeout policy. Qt supports duplicate server names on Windows; this child does not promise arbitrary custom-name collision refusal. Parent #131 retains normal-user Windows desktop startup, app command/state/orientation/search/capture/quit, actual second-user access-denial verification and hardware rendering. Transport success cannot close that desktop gate. Astra independently verifies the implementation and actual evidence.


## Accepted evidence (2026-10-13)
Closed with implementation9c42f08 and independent receipt9ec8ac2. Focused macOS transport and real-app discovery/identity/commands/capture/quit passed. Windows manual run38401749556 passed native pipe/helper/ACL tests at source9c42f08; report and binary verified. See docs/validation/local-transport.md for actual coverage and the empty Windows test stdout limitation. No desktop/GPU/second-user denial claim; parent131 remains Todo.

issues.body:
## Problem and result
Undo currently addresses committed document features while an active sketch stores disposable edits. Make accepted sketch operations undoable without changing unrelated committed document history.

## Scope
One bounded sketch-session journal for accepted entity, constraint, dimension and annotation edits through the existing authoritative commands. - Finish commits the resulting draft once; document Undo restores the previous sketch/solid state. Cancel preserves the pre-session document and its journal.
- Explicitly define behavior for a pending line point or inline value before traversing accepted draft history; preserve user work.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Create a snapped closed outline, undo and redo the last segment, then add/edit a dimension and undo/redo it. Verify relation IDs, profile closure and visible cue/session state. Finish, document Undo/Redo, re-enter/Cancel and save/reopen. Use one real-app workflow plus native shortcut dispatch; do not replace this with mock history tests.

issues.title: Support exterior topology for bilateral handle Trim and bridge
issues.body:
The accepted SRF-012 endpoint-contact arc/two-straight-line sheet is an independently authored ingredient. Its current paired XZ Trim gives one central seam opening, not the two distinct side sections required by the next handle bridge. Public source re-audit also describes mirrored lower spline geometry; straight lines were an Alloy simplification. Preserve this missing source-sized topology explicitly instead of counting the ingredient as full exterior compatibility.

Qualify an independently authored exterior with retained back arc, mirrored curved lower chain and intersecting rail, plus middle-plane handle sketch. Source exact coordinates, section-plane arrangement and interior/endpoint rail contacts remain unknown. Add only the curved-chain/contact/section support required by the declared fixture; do not silently substitute centerline semantics or invent exact-source claims. Keep stable source-derived face/edge IDs, meaningful rail/section edits, undo/reopen and atomic ambiguity refusal.

Acceptance: actual sketch-driven Trim produces two distinct usable side section boundaries about the middle ellipse; demonstrate that their topology can feed the planned side-to-middle-to-opposite-side handle Loft and eventual handle-bearing closed cell. Keep this geometric qualification separate from UI/source-exact parity. A central seam window or generic valid shell is not sufficient. If broader missing capabilities emerge, split explicit children before extending scope. The external surface-iron-2026-10-14/exterior-topology-audit-2026-10-14.md preserves public transcript/image provenance and uncertainties. SRF-015 retains the actual bridge feature implementation. TUT-018 must retain this prerequisite.

## Bounded feasibility checkpoint 2026-10-14
Independent Astra review supports returning this issue to Todo. Curved-boundary C0 patches do yield two distinct Trim loops, a bridge through a middle ellipse, and a capped handle-bearing solid, but measured seam mismatch reaches about 40 degrees. This is topology feasibility, not acceptable exterior quality or the retained tutorial workflow. A single G1 support-curtain experiment on unchanged base/edit fixtures fails: lower endpoint tangents depart 28-36 degrees from the prescribed tangent plane, global angular errors exceed 0.01 rad, and actual surface deviations reach 0.098 mm against 0.0003 mm. Valid BReps do not establish visual quality. This blocks that independently chosen fixture/constraint combination, not rail Loft generally. No tolerance relaxation or kernel sweep.

Next bounded scope: preflight endpoint tangent compatibility and explicitly qualify one independent compatible authored sketch fixture; retry the same evaluator and meaningful edit at unchanged limits before implementing retained controls. Reuse the existing Trim/bridge topology evidence only after the exterior quality gate passes. External evidence: deliverables/surface-iron-exterior-topology-2026-10-14/g1-curtain/. Full TUT-018 dependency remains.


The subsequent single endpoint-compatible preflight explicitly adds authored transverse tangent handles while preserving fit points. Analytic compatibility now passes and global G1 errors are low, but unchanged G0 limits fail at 0.002358/0.002609 mm versus 0.0003 mm; independent surface projections also fail. Astra verified the measurements. No Trim/bridge reuse or retained implementation was attempted. Park this evaluator/fixture quality blocker in Todo; do not infer impossibility of the broader workflow. External g1-compatible-preflight records the changed tangent intent. No further experiments in this increment.

## Active retained integration 2026-10-15
Independent review approved the exact tensor source-curve construction for a bounded port; actual-app acceptance is still required. The retained Trim integration must preserve degenerate collapsed-tip topology while excluding BRep_Tool::Degenerated edges from ordinary selectable boundary naming/counts. Do not use a length heuristic or publish fake curves. This narrow adaptation is necessary for the already-required two valid side openings, with existing ordinary edge naming preserved.


## Independently accepted 2026-10-15
Independently accepted at fc3ba9c for bounded actual solved Mirror-spline exterior and retained bilateral Trim. Exact tensor support,2faces/5ordinary edges,2validclosed handle loops, source edit/identity/history/reopen, rigid-frame invariance,43-call API and native3/3 pass. Default-opacity artifacts resolved without geometry changes; final14-call render replay/captures accepted. Naming is unique sampled correspondence against exact restrictions, not builder history. Actual bridge contacts and eventual closed cell remain explicitly in SRF-015/SRF-011/TUT-018. Trim latency and explicit translucency quality remain REL-026/REL-027. See docs/validation/surface-bilateral-rail-loft.md.

## Scope

Reuse established authoring/ownership commands; add component hierarchy reparent only as required. Independently authored four-solid fixture. Use existing ownership commands where already sufficient.

## Acceptance
- Four converted bodies remain identical solids at original world poses; each has named reusable definition/occurrence identity.
- Empty parent plus two piston children, root activation, source body edit, undo/redo/reopen and atomic cycle/dependency refusal.
- Shared API/native Browser actions and readable real-app hierarchy; exact physical drag only when separately proved.

Public research provenance and screenshots stay external in knowledge/tutorials/piston-subassemblies-2026-10-14/. The exact starting sample has no established public neutral asset; this is an independently authored adapted fixture, not exact source geometry. Parent requirements remain open.

Fixture connectivity is a required gate: both arms share one coaxial circular hinge, each arm has paired mounting centers separated by 180 mm along the declared copy axis, and the first telescoping piston connects one matching lower/upper mounting pair with circular end-eye axes. Moving its copied parent by the declared 180 mm reaches the opposite pair. Use independently authored dimensions and preserve native retained circular topology for later three Revolute plus one Cylindrical relationships. Four unrelated solids or separated bars without the shared hinge do not satisfy this fixture gate.

Independent Astra review accepts 3c0e208, integrated on main at 7bbf456. issues.title: Reuse coupled assembly evaluation within a preview update
issues.body:
## Scope split 2026-10-14
This implementation slice owns command-scoped evaluation reuse, unchanged solved geometry, atomic refusal and Revert. REL-011 preserves the original native drag profiling and responsiveness acceptance below; that portion is not completed by API evidence.

Split bounded follow-up from ASM-015; preserve functional acceptance separately from interaction performance.

## Observed evidence
The focused four-joint native test measured one preview event at 223 ms. The API creation movie also has repeated capture frames. These are observations, not a continuous input benchmark or proof of one common cause.

## Scope and acceptance
- Profile one short actual Upper Arm drag on the accepted 3R+1C fixture, separating input, authoritative solver evaluation, presentation rebuilding and capture overhead.
- Remove measured redundant work within a preview update where found. Any cached pose must be keyed to document revision, graph inputs and exact staged coordinate; source edits, undo/reopen, tab switches and Revert must invalidate it.
- Preserve independent original-joint/Pin checks and atomic failure. Do not relax geometric tolerances, skip relationships or replace solved motion with animation.
- Record before/after latency for a small representative event sequence and inspect actual native responsiveness. State hardware, capture mode and remaining limitations; no generic frame-rate claim from one event.
- Stop after a meaningful bounded improvement and focused regression evidence. Broader performance budgets remain REL-004; no unrelated renderer rewrite or benchmark project.

Evidence baseline: external deliverables/piston-coupled-ui-2026-10-14/native-01/.

## Profiling lead, source inspection 2026-10-14
`joint.previewAngle` calls AssemblyGraph::inspect to validate the proposed coordinate, then execute() refreshes presentation. presentationBodies() and presentationAssembly() independently solve the same graph. Profile these repeated solves and presentation rebuilds before adding caches or changing the solver. This is a source observation, not measured attribution of the 223 ms event; the issue remains Todo.
## Independent source review, proposed next increment
Astra traces additional repeated solves in Browser body population and state inspection. A bounded option is one owned AssemblyGraph evaluated result, with placed bodies and inspection derived from the same validated solve; retain existing wrappers. Memoize only within the outer execute/refresh scope, with exact effective authored snapshot, evaluation identity/generation and normalized stage override. Nested execute calls must recheck the key. Seed only after successful validation and preserve the previous stage on failure. Document revision alone is insufficient: preview candidates and transient coordinates change without it. Pending-reference presentation currently uses differing evaluation inputs; bypass those cases initially rather than silently sharing incompatible results. Relevant transitions include tab/document changes, source edit, history/reopen/prefix, component/type changes, Cancel/commit and Revert/Stop. Verify one solve for repeated identical presentation inputs plus existing pose/refusal checks and one measured before/after drag sample. This is a source-only proposal, not implementation or measured attribution; keep Todo until the cumulative native tutorial gate finishes.


## Independently accepted 2026-10-14
Independent Astra review accepted bd71bc0, integrated at 00b0990. Main app build and coupled core pass. Actual-app seven-joint API06 proves one solve per preview command and zero additional refresh solves, with valid signed poses, authored immutability, Revert and invalid-input refusal. Same-process combined/separate evaluation parity passes. This issue closes the bounded evaluation-reuse implementation; REL-011/#374 explicitly preserves native drag profiling and visual responsiveness acceptance in Todo. See docs/validation/assembly-preview-reuse.md.

issues.title: Evaluate retained arithmetic expressions in user length parameters
issues.body:
## Problem and result
Existing named lengths bind to real sketch and solid fields but their user values are numeric literals. Add a finishable expression slice: Width=40 mm and Length=Width*2 drive an editable rectangle/extrusion through existing stable-ID bindings.

## Scope
Expressions belong only to user length parameters in Change Parameters and document.parameterAdd/Update. Reuse existing named-ID bindings in model fields. Support decimal scalar literals, explicit mm/in literals, names, parentheses, unary signs and + - * /. Permit scalar arithmetic, length addition/subtraction, length times scalar and length divided by scalar. Reject length products/ratios, incompatible addition, functions and other units in this child. Bare numbers are scalar inside arithmetic; a final scalar is interpreted in the row's declared length unit. Thus Width*2 and Width+5 mm work; Width+5 refuses. This is an explicit Alloy policy where public unit-inference details remain unresolved.

Preserve literal-only saved documents. Formula rows retain source expression plus bound stable parameter UUIDs for identifier tokens; evaluated values are derived through one shared projection used by model bindings, UI and inspection. Repeated references, missing IDs and malformed bindings must not silently change dependencies. Rename updates token spellings while retaining IDs. Dependency-order evaluation rejects cycles and invalid arithmetic atomically, before ordinary geometry recompute. Preserve existing final length bounds. Keep the parser small and typed; no general scripting engine or speculative incremental evaluator.

## Acceptance and proportional verification

Create Width and derived Length, bind a rectangle dimension and extrusion through existing controls, then edit Width and verify dependent dimensions and solid volume. Include explicit inch/mm conversion and rename without rebinding. One focused core suite covers precedence, a cycle, invalid units/arithmetic, stable rename/load and refusal; one actual-app workflow covers atomic downstream failure, undo/redo and save/reopen. Inspect a readable GPU/parameter-table capture and one native expression cell edit. Keep API, Qt-delivered input and OS input qualifications separate; do not repeat unrelated tutorials.

## Retained parent scope

## Public evidence and design
Public parameter references parameters and paramedit support Width/Length equations and Expression/Value columns. Dated source URLs, public examples and unknowns stay external in knowledge/specs/par001-length-expression-slice-2026-10-14.md. Preview the circle contact and retain endpoint-on-circle plus tangent intent when the selected geometry is tangent; distinguish this ordinary click from the documented Shift-from-circle input.

- Refuse ambiguous tied branches or failed solves atomically; Escape cancels pending point/preview. Retain stable IDs and do not infer identity from approximate coordinates.

## Bounded split from SKT-021

Astra independently reviews implementation and actual app evidence.

issues.title: Reduce measured piston drag dispatch latency
issues.body:
## Measured problem
REL-011 records six actual Qt Upper Arm move dispatches on the accepted pinned 3R+1C piston fixture: 145.252–170.737 ms, median 159.925 ms, each with one graph solve. All exceed the predeclared 100 ms development-preview dispatch budget. Capture is outside timing; correctness, Pin and exact Revert pass. This is not a physical-input or frame-rate measurement.

## Bounded next step
Locate the dominant cost with a small targeted phase probe or profiler capture, then make one evidence-backed change in solve/presentation/input work. Reuse the exact saved fixture and native sequence. Do not weaken geometric tolerances, skip authoritative solves, relax constraints, or fabricate asynchronous completion. Preserve preview identity, original relations, Pin, authored data and exact Revert. Avoid speculative architecture or unchanged repeated runs; if two concrete hypotheses fail, preserve findings and split the remaining architecture requirement.

## Acceptance
Independent Astra review plus one matched before/after sequence on the same host/build recipe with capture inactive, all raw durations and honest phase limits. Target every measured dispatch at most 100 ms; if the target remains unmet, keep this issue open and report partial improvement. No smooth 60 Hz or physical-input claim. Parent REL-016 retains other model/startup/reopen/sketch budgets and general responsiveness.

## Bounded investigation stopped, 2026-10-14
Accepted diagnostic evidence at 9529c9d, not a latency fix. Same-source Release configuration passes correctness but median140.571/max150.151 ms still miss100 ms. One complete phase run identifies refresh/presentation130–175 ms versus solve/original-checks2–3 ms. A pose-only Browser/Timeline refresh experiment still exceeded budget and its optional selection test stopped before Revert; that behavior and test expansion were fully reverted. Only opt-in existing-flag timing diagnostics remain. Independent Astra reviewed evidence/revert; issue returns Todo after two cost hypotheses. Do not repeat unchanged configuration/profiler/pose-refresh attempts. Next attempt needs a distinct source-backed presentation-cost hypothesis. Receipt: docs/validation/assembly-native-drag-profile.md.

issues.title: Avoid full geometry recomputation for display-only visibility changes
issues.body:
During corrected iron replay, hiding a body blocks the UI for tens of seconds. A one-second process sample shows feature.visibility -> CadDocument::evaluateCandidateFromPrefix -> GeometryKernel::evaluateDocument -> SurfaceTrim::evaluate -> OCCT Splitter on the main thread, CPU96%. Existing REL-016/#419 retains timings.

Find the smallest safe way to reuse evaluated geometry on visibility-only changes while preserving authored visibility, Browser/viewport/API consistency, exact undo/redo, component/consumed-body behavior and save/reopen. Do not infer visibility from geometry or skip legitimate dependency work for dimensional changes.

Acceptance: on the actual corrected iron model, show/hide does not re-run Trim/Loft; rendered visibility and authored state agree. Focused core metadata/undo test plus real-app capture and measured command timing. Keep asynchronous geometry evaluation/cancellation as separate broader work; this issue does not claim all UI freezes are resolved.

## Independently accepted 2026-10-17
Integrated e555907. Strict visibility-only document admission reuses immutable evaluated geometry and producer-based flags. Focused document_append regression passes. Actual corrected-iron hide/show improves from41.718/47.911s to335.8/345.2ms with explicit visibility_only branch witnesses, unchanged geometry/assembly summaries, exact restored authored state and actual GPU captures. Astra independently reviewed source/tests/raw ledger/images. See docs/validation/visibility-only-evaluation.md. Active Combine preview, geometry edits and cold reopen remain broader REL-016 responsiveness scope.

issues.title: Explicitly repair a retained planar inset after an upstream boundary change
issues.body:
## Concrete missing workflow
Editing the enclosure port Cut to the approved clearance genuinely changes the same retained Split cap outer boundary from18 to16edges. The planarInsetV1 exact edge-set guard correctly refuses the old outerLoopId. There is no boundary-reselection repair or rollback/suppression workflow to repair it in place. TUT-035 can rebuild its four-feature rim tail as a documented adaptation, but that does not implement repair.

## Bounded scope
Define and implement explicit user/agent reselection of the current outer boundary on the same retained producer/body/face. Preserve the intended offset distance, authored offset/profile identity where meaningful, and atomically validate downstream Join/Fillet/Combine. If downstream selections genuinely changed, present an explicit repair requirement instead of nearest-coordinate matching or silently dropping operations. Keep old planarInsetV1 exact semantics; do not silently weaken its guard. UI and local commands must share the same document transaction.

## Acceptance
Use original final enclosure plus port Cut305a8352-674c-4568-bf72-da34ec14c45c endOffsetMm=-1.5. Explain the changed rim boundary, explicitly select the new boundary, preview complete downstream result, and support Cancel, commit, undo/redo, save/reopen. Preserve nominal reference payload and prior valid document on refusal. Record new/repaired selections and changed identities. Verify actual captured controls as well as geometry; general automatic topology repair is outside this bounded child.

## Evidence
External deliverables/enclosure-cumulative-2026-10-17/inset-boundary-diff-01 records two evaluated prefixes, identical support/frame, actual edge geometry/identity difference and independent Astra diagnosis. TUT-035 owns the approved model variant; HIS-002 retains broader persistent-reference scope.

issues.title: Keep final body organization out of edited-feature preview prefixes
issues.body:
## Problem and result
Editing the enclosure port Cut before the case Split and previewing endOffsetMm=-1.5 fails with `Renamed local body is no longer active; repair or undo the upstream edit`. The full 29-feature candidate is valid. The edit preview also evaluates a temporary history prefix ending at the edited feature, but that prefix retains final-document `bodyNames` and `objectOwners` entries for bodies created later. The later Top rename therefore appears stale only in the temporary prefix.

## Bounded scope
Exclude final-document organization metadata from temporary edited-feature evaluation prefixes until its referenced local bodies exist. Cover both renamed and reparented later-created bodies. Preserve the strict full-document body-name and ownership guards, saved metadata, feature IDs/order, geometry and normal reference checks. Do not change geometry reference lineage or weaken the inset/topology guard.

## Acceptance criteria
- On the saved 29-feature enclosure-through-snaps model, edit Cut `305a8352-674c-4568-bf72-da34ec14c45c` to `endOffsetMm=-1.5`; preview succeeds when later Split bodies `Top` and `Bottom` are renamed or reparented.
- Preview followed by Cancel leaves authored organization metadata, feature IDs/order and evaluated geometry unchanged.
- Preview followed by Commit preserves those IDs and intended names/owners; Undo/Redo and save/reopen restore the corresponding state and geometry.
- A focused regression verifies that truly unavailable full-document name/owner references still fail through the existing guard.
- The separate TUT-035 real-application clearance runner remains the cumulative geometry/product gate; this issue does not establish connector clearance or downstream rim acceptance.

## Proposed verification and evidence
Add focused history-prefix coverage and extend the real Alloy API replay for edit, preview, Cancel, commit, Undo/Redo and save/reopen using the external accepted enclosure fixture. Record preview result, full authored metadata and feature identity comparisons. Run the root-owned clearance runner only as its separate cumulative TUT-035 gate.

## Evidence
The 2026-10-17 `clearance-prefix-02` transcript reproduces the preview failure. The external `inset-boundary-diff-01` old/new prefix diagnostics show the same named bodies and successful full 29-feature evaluations after the cut edit; the error is specific to the temporary preview prefix, not the valid full candidate.

## Accepted 2026-10-17
Only the temporary edited-feature preview prefix drops final bodyNames/objectOwners; the full candidate retains them. Focused real-app regression passed preview, Cancel, commit, later-body identity/name/owner preservation, undo/redo and save/reopen. The original 29-feature enclosure Cut preview and edit now pass through real Alloy with exact authored identity. See docs/validation/extrude-edit-preview-prefix.md and external deliverables/enclosure-cumulative-2026-10-17/extrude-prefix-regression-01 plus clearance-prefix-03. The connector-clearance model, rim and printing exports remain TUT-035; this child closes only the preview-prefix failure.

issues.title: Keep expensive Surface Extrude preview off the UI thread
issues.body:
## Observed failure
The real corrected-iron from-blank recording edits a retained per-profile Surface Extrude to add the bottom curve. `command.preview` takes 119.4 seconds while synchronous candidate evaluation runs on the Qt UI thread; the editor is unresponsive during that time. Earlier opening/preview was ~81.1 seconds. Evidence: external deliverables/iron-reassessment-2026-10-17/candidate-13-from-blank-recording/{transcript.json,current-operation.json,iron-creation.mp4} after the bounded run finishes. The final geometry and native/STL outputs succeeded, but recording.stop refused after a gap over 300 frame slots during the UI-thread stall; candidate13 exited nonzero with no accepted movie. This is a runtime usability and validation blocker. REL-016/#419 owns broad responsiveness; this child owns the concrete UI-blocking preview path.

## Bounded implementation
Trace `AlloyWindow::previewSurfaceExtrude` (`src/SurfaceExtrudeControls.cpp`) and `CadDocument::prepareCandidate`. The current edited-feature preview evaluates the full draft, then reevaluates a truncated prefix. Eliminate redundant work where semantics permit, and make expensive evaluation nonblocking to the Qt event loop with explicit pending/completed/failed command state. Keep authoritative document commits, revision guards, preview/Cancel, stable identities, and the local control API's reliable completion behavior. Display progress/busy state and provide safe cancellation if the kernel/evaluation path supports it; do not claim cancellation by merely dropping an in-flight result. Preserve GPU interaction and avoid data races in OCCT/Qt objects.

## Acceptance
One focused real-app run on the saved corrected-iron fixture demonstrates the UI stays responsive during the slow preview (e.g. timer heartbeat and basic navigation/cancel behavior appropriate to the chosen semantics), with the same evaluated preview/commit and exact undo/reopen as before. Record wall time and phase cost separately from UI responsiveness; the fix must not just raise the API timeout, spin a nested event loop, weaken geometry checks, or fabricate completion. Add a small targeted test for the command-state/revision contract and independent architecture/code review. If a safe async migration is broader than one issue, split an exact child and preserve this blocker as Todo until the user-facing gate passes.

## Parent
REL-016/#419; corrected iron TUT-034/#470 can retain functional/movie evidence but is not human-ready until this responsiveness gate is addressed.

issues.title: Keep long Boundary Fill commit responsive and recordable
issues.body:
## Observed failure
The corrected-iron from-blank run reaches the independently accepted final solid, but its `command.commit` for Boundary Fill consumes 94.4577 seconds synchronously on the Qt UI thread. The recording then refuses a clip after `Frame gap exceeded 300 slots`; the saved native model/STL remain valid. External evidence: `deliverables/iron-reassessment-2026-10-17/candidate-13-from-blank-recording/{README.md,receipt.json,long-command-timings.json,transcript.json}`. This operation alone exceeds a 60-second frame-gap window, so the Surface Extrude-only REL-033 fix cannot establish a complete responsive tutorial recording.

## Bounded scope
Profile the final Boundary Fill cell commit on the saved accepted four-tool fixture. Keep the GUI event loop responsive while exact authoritative evaluation completes, with explicit pending/completed/failed state, stale revision/selection guards, one atomic history commit and no concurrent kernel use that races live viewport topology. Preserve selected-cell identity, Remove Tools behavior, final geometry, undo/redo and native reopen. Do not weaken the Boolean kernel, raise the recorder's gap limit as a substitute for responsiveness, or advertise a blocked app as a successful human workflow. Reuse the serial-worker/completion contract established by REL-033 where appropriate; avoid a second incompatible task framework.

## Verification
One bounded real-app replay of the saved final Boundary Fill fixture shows a repaint/status/navigation heartbeat during computation and an exact accepted solid after completion. Measure wall time separately from event-loop response. Check Cancel/result discard and stale session behavior where supported, plus one focused command-state test. Independent architecture/geometry review before closing. Recording acceptance belongs to TUT-034/#470 and must be separately replayed after both long-operation blockers are addressed.

## Parent/dependencies
REL-016/#419 owns cumulative responsiveness. REL-033/#476 provides the first serial worker/completion infrastructure; start this child after that contract is accepted. TUT-034/#470 depends on this before a successful complete creation movie can be claimed.

Preserve exact cell IDs, volumes, candidate previews, selected-cell identity and Remove Tools behavior. Admit results only for the matching document, revision, session, tools, owner and generation. Let users navigate, inspect pending state and Cancel while it evaluates; do not claim OCCT interruption if Cancel only discards results. Preserve safe serialization with final commit and other worker operations.

## Verification
One saved-fixture real-app replay measures UI heartbeat, status and navigation through initial enumeration and compares the resulting cells/selection and final solid to the accepted fixture. Focused pending/stale/Cancel test, exact history and reopen, and independent review. Do not repeat the complete iron tutorial movie just to test this child; TUT-034 owns that cumulative recording.

Reuse the established worker protocol where practical; do not reduce geometry checks to hide latency.

## Verification
Open the saved corrected-iron model through the real app with a repaint/status/navigation heartbeat, compare authored feature IDs and final solid/face-edge references with the accepted fixture, then inspect undo/history and save. Cover one failed/cancelled load leaving the original document intact with a focused test. Independent review before closing. This is separate from the corrected tutorial creation movie and cross-platform runtime gates.

issues.body:
## Observed result
REL-036/#479 moves the saved corrected-iron native Open's 30.607-second evaluation off the Qt UI thread. Pending status calls and viewport navigation stay responsive. The terminal completion response still takes 1.278542 seconds, including GUI-thread adoption, presentation/rebind and serialization. ## Bounded scope
Profile the accepted large-model completion into document adoption, viewport actor rebuild, Browser/timeline refresh, Fit and API response serialization. Retain atomic document replacement, exact geometry and reference IDs, same-tab behavior, history reset and failure/Cancel preservation. Reduce avoidable main-thread presentation work or stage it safely across event-loop ticks while reporting explicit terminal completion only when the document is ready. Do not rerun kernel evaluation, weaken geometry checks or claim a global latency budget from pending-only metrics.

## Verification
One bounded saved-iron Open replay measures GUI heartbeat through final adoption separately from background evaluation, compares exact authored/geometry/history and inspects readable final presentation. A focused regression covers completion identity and no partial visible document. Independent review before closure. Broader startup/STEP import remain outside this child.

## Parent
REL-016/#419 cumulative responsiveness; REL-036/#479 provides the accepted asynchronous Open foundation.

## Independently accepted 2026-10-17
The saved corrected-iron Open now reuses worker-evaluated exact body bounds for final Fit, with a kernel fallback for missing/invalid bounds. Current-build terminal polling fell from 520–578 ms to 469–470 ms; Fit fell from about 70 ms to 9–12 ms. The concurrent app.state probe recorded 265 successful samples with one 415.5 ms final-window stall. Exact authored state, same tab ID/count, clean history reset, metadata edit undo/redo and readable GPU capture pass. The full document.open terminal result and failure/Cancel contracts remain intact. Astra independently accepted the bounded code/evidence; a roughly 0.42 s final pause remains. See docs/validation/open-final-presentation.md. Broader REL-016 and other-platform runtime remain open.

issues.title: Keep historical sketch Edit responsive and establish background Finish commands

This bounded increment moves private prefix evaluation and changed-sketch candidate evaluation to the existing serial worker, with shared command/session state, stale-result guards, Cancel-as-result-discard and visible errors. The exact saved-fixture Finish witness is retained by REL-042; this issue does not claim it.

On the saved pre-bottom iron checkpoint, historical Edit submitted in 40.617 ms and evaluated for 53.331 s off-thread. Focused tests cover Finish success/failure, visible error and retry, cancellation, one history transaction, new-sketch behavior, and shared normalized-adoption regression. Astra independently reviewed the source. The stale full-document operation result that exceeded the control client bound was corrected; app.state returned 673,794 bytes in the next real run. REL-042 must establish reliable initial native activation and run the exact bottom-line Finish through the saved iron checkpoint, then compare geometry/references/history/reopen and responsiveness. No full tutorial or downstream suffix rerun is required solely for this child. REL-016/#419 retains cumulative responsiveness.

issues.title: Make Surface Trim preview match committed partition across viewport mesh states
issues.body:
## Observed mismatch
The saved corrected-iron panel Trim live preview used viewport-tessellated target bounds and reported sketch-normal projection extent about ±70.4769 mm. The accepted committed Trim recomputed from fresh unmeshed geometry and used ±118.2178 mm, with different preview region areas. The REL-038 private-worker partition matches the committed regions and projection exactly, exposing a pre-existing preview-versus-commit inconsistency. Evidence: accepted candidate14 transcript entries 115/121/123 and external validation/rel038-responsive-trim-2026-10-17/saved-fixtures/ first stopped replay.

## Bounded work
Make Surface Trim partition bounds and region presentation independent of incidental viewport triangulation. Use a stable geometry-based bounding method or a deliberately controlled tessellation policy on both live and private sources. Preserve exact committed removal semantics, target/tool identity, region ancestry and stable references. A preview must show the regions and extent that OK will actually commit, even after view navigation or first mesh generation. Do not change kernel geometry merely to make a stale preview oracle pass.

## Verification
Use the saved panel checkpoint with and without viewport tessellation; compare preview region provenance/area/projection to the exact committed result, then verify one history operation, Undo/Redo and native reopen. Add a focused bound-policy regression and independently inspect before/after app captures. Avoid a full tutorial replay solely for this child.

## Dependency
REL-038/#481 establishes the background partition/commit path. REL-016/#419 retains cumulative responsiveness.

issues.title: Record the corrected iron creation with responsive UI throughout

Record actual mouse/key/API commands and frame cadence, status/navigation/GUI heartbeat at former long stages, exact stage ledger, native model, STL/STEP and final solid. Preserve source-step inputs and accepted geometry; do not silently skip stages or conceal waits by inserting repeated frames without noting them. Include the meaningful source edit/Undo/Redo/reopen check if already part of the accepted script. Stop at the first product or harness failure, diagnose before a bounded rerun, and avoid repeated full movies for cosmetic changes.

Independently review captured visual state, transcript/frame gaps, geometry and source/binary identity. The frozen replay stopped at its first failure: document.exportStl blocked the UI command path for 2.035 s and the actual frame gap was 2.088 s, over the 2 s gate. No encoder/capture failure was observed. The final solid and STL matched the accepted candidate, but normal final save, STEP, postmovie source edit and reopen did not run. After REL-047/#493, unchanged candidate16 completed all 44 creation stages with a 686 ms maximum actual-frame gap, responsive pending status/navigation/heartbeat, exact authored/evaluated recipe and ancestry under independent 156-ID mapping, byte-identical STL, checked STEP, and postmovie source edit/Undo/Redo/reopen. External gallery: `../Alloy-reference-records/demos/2026-10-13/index.html#surface-iron-responsive`; in-repo receipt: `docs/validation/iron-responsive-cumulative.md`. The failed candidate15 remains preserved. Physical input, other platforms/models and exact public gesture/dimension parity remain separate.

issues.title: Keep large-model STL export responsive
issues.body:
## Observed stall
The first REL-046 corrected-iron cumulative replay stopped at the frozen 2 s actual-frame-gap gate. `document.exportStl` took 2034.890 ms synchronously on the UI command path, across an actual frame interval of 2088 ms. No encoder/capture failure occurred. The resulting STL is valid, but the full replay did not reach STEP, postmovie source edit or reopen. Independent review found `MeshExport::writeStl` invoked directly from the UI handler and doing geometry copy/meshing/serialization/atomic publication there. Evidence: external candidate15 `failure-diagnosis.json`, operation metrics and frame events.

## Bounded work
Move a committed single-solid STL export's expensive kernel/mesh/file work to a private worker with explicit pending/completion semantics. Keep the existing millimeter binary-STL geometry, validation, structured errors, destination/atomic-publish policy, and shared API/UI command behavior. Snapshot only immutable evaluated geometry/parameters on the GUI thread; measure that boundary. Guard completion against stale document/tab/revision and cancellation as result-discard; do not publish a stale export. Keep one export job at a time if needed. Avoid speculative generalized export framework.

## Verification
On the saved corrected iron, measure submit, pending status/navigation/GUI heartbeat and final publication separately; require real frame gaps under the REL-046 2 s gate. Compare STL bytes or canonical triangle/volume/bounds/closedness to accepted output, inspect cancellation/stale behavior, errors and no partial destination, with a focused test for the core contract. One saved-model real-app gate before rerunning the full 44-stage movie. Independent source and evidence review.

## Dependency
REL-036 supplies the established serial worker pattern. REL-046/#492 waits on this fix; REL-016/#419 retains broader responsiveness.

## Ownership
Explicit remainder split from SKT-099/#518; the first slice covers authored line/circle/arc/point. Do not infer full sketch-family parity from either bounded issue alone.
## Finishable split — 2026-10-18
This active slice qualifies whole-entity Delete for authored ellipse, conic, fit/control splines, and an atomic grouped/derived refusal. It does not implement group removal. The original grouped/derived requirement is preserved as linked Todo SKT-141 (constructor groups), SKT-142 (Mirror/Offset groups), and SKT-143 (projected/link ownership). Their dependencies and native/geometry gates remain explicit. Dated public triage is external at knowledge/specs/skt102-delete-triage-2026-10-18.md.

Authored whole-entity ellipse, conic, fitSpline and controlSpline Delete now removes owned axes and unshared points while preserving shared point identities and unrelated relations. Canvas Delete, context popup, and sketch-list Delete use the shared command; final native Qt test observes popup activation and closure, 3/3 passed in 2.102 s. Real-entrypoint 122-call API fixture checks all four curves, fit-point removal distinction, exact Undo/Redo, ellipse-axis refusal, atomic slot-owner refusal, valid closed downstream circle extrusion of 5654.866776461628 mm³ and authored save/reopen. Apple M4 GPU captures inspected; independent Sol review accepted. Generated-group/derived deletion remains SKT-141–143/#567–569, not part of this accepted slice. issues.title: Retain actual Polygon placement snaps and relations
issues.body:
## Bounded result
Retain one genuine Polygon placement anchor in each of the three modes. Inscribed and Circumscribed anchor their center; Edge anchors the first endpoint of its fixed base edge. This is the first-anchor snap/relation remainder of SKT-093/#498 under ADV-005/#101.

## Acceptance
- Acquire supported origin, authored-point or line-midpoint snaps with a cue only when the relation will be retained. Grid alignment is a coordinate choice, not an authored relation.
- A snapped anchor stores stable source references and Coincident/Midpoint relation; an unsnapped anchor may remain explicitly fixed. Polygon vertices maintain exact relative size/orientation from the solved anchor, rather than carrying absolute vertex fixes that prevent upstream motion.
- Move the upstream reference and verify the Polygon, its closed profile and one downstream extrusion follow. Count/size edits preserve the anchor relation or refuse atomically; keep surviving boundary IDs and dependent constraints.
- Missing, ambiguous, self-referential and removed targets refuse without changing authored geometry or history. Verify native cue/click, shared control result, Undo/Redo and save/reopen. Use dated public Polygon evidence and distinguish input, geometry and visual acceptance.

## Explicit split
SKT-093/#498 supplies the retained three-mode foundation. [SKT-105/#528](https://github.com/rje/Alloy/issues/528) owns second-driver snaps: radial vertex or edge midpoint in center modes and second base endpoint in Edge, including size/angle ownership and conflict behavior. This issue does not claim that second-driver behavior.

issues.title: Audit intrinsic cost of every supported v1 command after packaging
issues.body:
## Sequencing and result
After the v1 functional and packaging gates are complete, audit the intrinsic cost of every supported v1 command and make measured inefficiencies actionable. Moving a slow operation off the UI thread is a responsiveness mitigation, not proof that its implementation is efficient. This gate complements REL-004 budgets and REL-016 interactive responsiveness.

## Acceptance
- Build a versioned inventory of supported v1 command IDs and representative real-document fixtures. Include cold and warm runs, declared hardware, document/feature counts, p50/p95 or stable ranges, and separate UI dispatch, sketch solve, dependency recompute, geometry kernel, tessellation, save/export and redraw time where applicable. Avoid exhaustive option combinations without a material risk.
- Reproduce the corrected-iron simple Cut and other known slow fixtures, along with ordinary sketch/solid/exchange commands. Compare the measured work to geometric complexity and REL-004 budgets; identify avoidable repeated recompute, redundant kernel calls, unnecessary remeshing/serialization, poor data structures and synchronous waits. An asynchronous wrapper alone does not resolve a slow intrinsic path.
- For each measured inefficiency, create a bounded linked fix issue with the exact fixture, baseline and acceptance target. Complete those issues, rerun identical fixtures, verify geometry/authored history/undo/save/export invariants, and record improved timing. Keep genuine kernel-heavy or hardware-limited exceptions explicit and evidence-based.
- Publish a concise command-by-command audit table with status, evidence path and remaining accepted limitations. Use the real application/control API and hardware GPU; keep build, API, geometry, native interaction and visual evidence distinct. Run proportional focused tests rather than repeated full-suite passes.

## Dependencies
- REL-004/#83 defines practical performance budgets; REL-016 owns interactive responsiveness.
- Begin after v1 functionality/scope and all-platform package/runtime gates (REL-030, REL-003, GATE-005, REL-018) have been reconciled. Do not pull this audit ahead of the current modeling and packaging burndown.
